<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3e5bfa69348cd8dd7067ac3c734f753875d4bc4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `425cc7db21b4e5ac643f0ae4bf7994e900b82c4b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/temporary-password-length.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users-password-length.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users-manager-pass.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users-invite-link.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users-invite-delivery-failure.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users-account-invitation.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/account-invitation-marker.webcontainer.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/durability-swallow-repair.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (`getAuthContext`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts (the range's writer into better-auth), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.test.ts, .changeset/25932-import-users-temporary-password-length.md (level and declaration lines only, under ②), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs and scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (the gates the changeset answers to), AGENTS.md §3 (the convention)

Read against `main` at the PR's base `05f7758f` (PR #25927 / `1d2a246c`, create-user's sizing, is already in it) with the net diff overlaid; the card's body and all three comments (triage `6408548839`, claim `6411247608`, dev report `6412451931`); and the 49 check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`IdentityImportDeps` gains a REQUIRED `getAuthContext()` — a narrowing, and correctly declared as one.** The interface is on the package entry: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts:61` is `export * from './admin-import-users.js'`, and `package.json` `exports["."]` serves `dist/index.*`, so `IdentityImportDeps` and `runAdminImportUsers` are public. The interface is the input parameter of `runAdminImportUsers` (contravariant position): adding a required member shrinks the set of deps objects a host may pass. Nothing new is accepted. Compile-time, a TypeScript host without the member no longer type-checks; runtime, a JavaScript host without it has every import refused at the new read (`deps.getAuthContext` is not a function, caught, mapped) before any row is written. That is the accept-set NARROWING `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` names, not a widening. The member's type, `Promise<{ password: Pick<AuthContextLike['password'], 'config'> }>`, is the minimum the sizing needs and is satisfied both by `AuthManager.getAuthContext()` (`Promise<any>`, `auth-manager.ts:4049`) and by the test mocks' `{ password: { config } }` literal. Right. The HTTP request shape of `POST /admin/import-users` is unchanged, so the PR body's "no request shape is widened or refused" is also right.

2. **Every in-repo constructor of the deps supplies it.** At the base, the files naming `runAdminImportUsers` or `IdentityImportDeps` anywhere under `packages/` outside `node_modules`/`dist` are exactly nine: `admin-import-users.ts`, `auth-plugin.ts` (the one non-test caller, the route at `:3766`) and seven test files. All nine are in the PR's file list, and every one of the deps literals in them gains `getAuthContext` (route and real-manager fixtures wire `manager.getAuthContext()`; the three mock fixtures answer better-auth's default 8–128 range). No package outside plugin-auth, no example and no app constructs these deps (the only out-of-package mentions are `CHANGELOG.md` prose). Right; the compiler would have named any miss, and `Type Check · workspace` / `Type Check · consumer gates` on the head are the gate verdicts for that (see ③).

3. **Exactly one reader of the length range.** Both doors read the range from the same object by the same expression: create-user `admin-user-endpoints.ts:724` `(await deps.getAuthContext()).password.config`, and the import (new) `temporaryPasswordLength((await deps.getAuthContext()).password.config)`. Both `getAuthContext` deps are wired by `AuthPlugin` to `AuthManager.getAuthContext()`, which returns better-auth's own `$context`. The other `minPasswordLength`/`maxPasswordLength` sites in non-test source are the range's WRITERS into better-auth (`auth-manager-auth-instance.ts:375-378`, `auth-plugin.ts:2083-2087` mapping the ADR-0069 settings), and `admin-user-endpoints.ts:378-383` consumes the same `lengthPolicy` value already read at `:724` for the explicit-password check. No second reader (no settings read, no config read, no env read) was added. Right, and it satisfies the claim's `⛔ no second reader of the range` ruling.

4. **The sizing has one home and its public surface did not move.** `temporaryPasswordLength` was a module-private (non-exported) function in `admin-user-endpoints.ts`; it is now the exported function of the new internal module `temporary-password-length.ts`, which `index.ts` does not re-export (the barrel is untouched in the diff). So the package's public surface gains nothing for it. `mapAuthApiError`, `AuthContextLike` and `generateTemporaryPassword` were already exported from `admin-user-endpoints.ts` (and on the barrel) at the base; the import only adds imports of them. Right.

5. **The formula and the default.** `min(max(16, minPasswordLength), maxPasswordLength)` is the card's wanted formula, byte for byte the create-user one. With better-auth's default range (8–128) it is 16, pinned by test ③ (real stack) and by the mock fixtures' comment. Right; the card's second acceptance line holds.

6. **Read once, before any write; refusal with nothing created.** The read sits after the `createUser` capability check and before the `protocol` is built and `runImport` runs, so it precedes every row write and every `sys_user` update, and runs once per request rather than per row. A throw is mapped by `mapAuthApiError(error, 'import-users failed')`, the same mapping create-user uses for the same read (`:725-727`): a plain `Error` becomes `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`. The new unit pin verifies `createUser` and `engine.update` are never called. A `dryRun` request also pays the read; that is acceptable (an unreadable auth context is a deployment fault, and a dry run that silently reported "would create" under it would misreport). Right.

7. **`auto` policy's no-channel fallback.** The card read it from code only; the PR measures it (test ②, real stack, no email service): the fallback resolves `plan.kind === 'temporary'` and takes the same `generateTemporaryPassword(temporaryLength)` branch. Right.

8. **The red-first test pins the route's wiring, not just the function.** `admin-import-users-password-length.test.ts` mounts the plugin's real `registerAuthRoutes` over a real `AuthManager` + SQLite, so a route that forgot `getAuthContext` would red it. The one stand-in is the admin gate's session read. Right; this is the test the card's acceptance asked for (minimum above 16 → the row's password meets it and the user signs in with it: tests ① and ② assert length 24 and `sign-in/email` 200).

9. **Boundary noted, not a defect.** `generateTemporaryPassword` floors its length at 12 (unchanged, shared with create-user). A deployment with `maxPasswordLength` below 12 would get a 12-character password that better-auth then refuses, on the import and on create-user alike. That is inherited from #25927's sizing, which the card's ruling says to follow exactly ("the way #25824 sizes create-user's"), so it is out of this card's scope and consistent across the doors. Recorded for the seat; no change asked.

10. **Security family.** The change only raises or caps the length of a generated credential to the configured policy; nothing about delivery, storage, the must-change gate or the admin gate moves. No new information leaves the door (the 500 message mirrors create-user's existing mapping). No reproduction recipe is recorded here.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/25932-import-users-temporary-password-length.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-auth': patch`. The diff publishes only from `@objectstack/plugin-auth`. Right.
- Declaration lines, line-initial and identical on the PR body and the changeset: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The narrowing is the required deps member (① item 1). No spec key, authorable value, metadata type or default changes, so `none` is the right kind, and under AGENTS.md §3 `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The changeset carries `**BREAKING** for a host that calls runAdminImportUsers itself`, a Before / Now / Fix block (the fix: pass `getAuthContext` wired to `AuthManager.getAuthContext()`), and the title carries `!`. This is the same shape the sibling #25927 (`1d2a246c`) landed with. Right.
- ADR-0087: `<!-- adr-0087: not-required (runtime-interface-only packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts#IdentityImportDeps) ... -->`. Checked against the gate's four predicates: the `<path>#<Symbol>` resolves to an exported `interface` at HEAD; its declaration site is a plain `.ts` (not `*.zod.ts`, not `packages/spec/src/contracts/**`, not an object definition); it is not a Zod projection; and no metadata surface references it in code (the only files naming `IdentityImportDeps` are the nine plugin-auth sources above). The body carries no FROM → TO migration prescription, so the inherited `no-migration-prescription` refusal does not bite. Right.
- Gate verdicts: `Check Changeset` (the job that runs `check-changeset-no-major` — launch-window guard, level axis and lockstep — and the real `check-adr-0087-registration` scan) is `success` on the head, twice (the two check-runs of that name). `Lint · docs & code guards`, which hosts the changeset-family self-tests, is `success`.
- `check-changeset-no-major` constraints: no `major` is introduced; `none` grades its one entry `patch` and moves no `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` baseline (none is in the diff); the `(narrowing)` arm beside `no` is well-formed (`no (widening)` would be the malformed one). Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report (`6412451931`): `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer there. The flags its summary raises, each answered:

- **Clause-② measured `no (narrowing)` against the claim's expected `yes`.** The deviation is correct (① item 1): a required member on an exported deps interface is an accept-set narrowing, and the claim itself said "expected; the dev measures". The title `!`, the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker follow from it and are all present.
- **Required rather than optional.** Agreed. An optional member needs an absent-branch fallback, and the only fallback is the unsized 16, which is the defect; required makes the compiler name every host. The PR body's acceptance note says the same.
- **Worktree / branch note** (harness branch re-pointed at `origin/main 05f7758f` in a dedicated worktree; no unique commits lost). The branch is `claude/project-thread-brnfvi`, the claim's identity record; the check-run `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` is `success`, so the claim/branch pairing holds.
- **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally** (prerequisite: every package's `dist`). It is hosted by `Build Core` in `ci.yml` (`:2906`); see the check-run roll-up below for its conclusion on the head.
- **Three first-pass local reds re-run green** (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dts-closure`, `check:type-check-debt`), all prerequisite faults. CI's own runs decide: `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` and `Type Check · debt ledger` are `success` on the head.
- **Out-of-scope finding (class a): `authz-probe-blind-spot.test.ts` red on `main`'s dogfood battery at the base** (`packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts`, control `handleI18nRequest` 3 → 4, since `69fa23d6` / #25956). Not this diff (`packages/runtime` untouched). On the head the `Dogfood Regression Gate` aggregate is `success` and its three matrix shards are `skipped` (path-filtered), so CI did not re-measure it here. Escalated to the seat as a `main`-side item for a card of its own; it does not bear on this PR's verdict.
- **Author.** The PR is authored by `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay-written via the card thread `session_01A5wzhKHa98KsGQNHM9Z3Tq`); no non-relay author note is needed.
- **Check-runs on `425cc7db` (49 in total).** Every completed non-skipped run concluded `success`: Auto Label, Check Changeset (x2), Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, filter. `Build Core` is `success`, so `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, the one derived gate the dev could not measure locally, is measured green by CI. Skipped (path- or opt-in-gated): the UI jobs, the dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness. No run has concluded other than `success` or `skipped`. **Still `in_progress` at render time (2026-10-26T09:24Z, all started 09:16Z):** `Test Core (1/8)` through `Test Core (8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace` and `Type Check · consumer gates`. Those ten are the CI verdicts for the plugin-auth vitest run and for the compile check of ① item 2; the dev measured both locally (3726 passed; typecheck exit 0, `check:test-typecheck` OK) and this review verified every constructor by reading, so the verdict below rests on the diff and does not wait for them, but the seat must not arm auto-merge until all ten conclude `success`, and a non-success conclusion on any of them re-opens this record on this head.
